results.name: Achilles and the Tortoise
results.statement: Finite distance is traversed in finite steps using geometric series summation.
results.formal_proposition: Linear kinematic intersection d_meet = v_A * t = d0 + v_T * t refutes the assertion that Achilles never catches the tortoise.

results.name: Russell Set Paradox
results.statement: Set of all sets that do not contain themselves creates ungrounded self-reference.
results.formal_proposition: Unrestricted comprehension R = {x | x not in x} yields R in R <=> not(R in R), which is logically refutable.

results.name: Barber Paradox
results.statement: Barber shaves all and only those who do not shave themselves.
results.formal_proposition: In a first-order relational structure, forall x (shaves(b, x) <=> not(shaves(x, x))) is first-order unsatisfiable.
assumptions: Barber is a member of the domain

results.name: Liar Paradox
results.statement: Sentence asserting its own falsehood ("This statement is false").
results.formal_proposition: A proposition asserting T <=> not(T) is unsatisfiable in classical bivalent truth systems.

results.name: Grelling-Nelson Paradox
results.statement: Is "heterological" (a word not describing itself) heterological?
results.formal_proposition: Semantic predicate Het(w) <=> not(Applies(w, w)) applied reflexively to Het yields Het <=> not(Het), refutable in bivalent semantics.
assumptions: Words can be predicates over words
constraints: applies is a 2-place relation on words

results.name: Curry Paradox
results.statement: Self-referential conditional implies arbitrary falsehood without negation.
results.formal_proposition: Sentence C asserting C => F allows proving arbitrary falsehood F via contraction (modus ponens with self-premise).

results.name: Berry Paradox
results.statement: The smallest positive integer not definable in under eleven words.
results.formal_proposition: Kolmogorov complexity bound: Integer N having complexity K(N) >= L cannot have description length < L.

results.name: Richard Paradox
results.statement: Diagonalization over all definable real numbers.
results.formal_proposition: If all definable reals in (0, 1) are enumerated, diagonal element r differs at the n-th position from the n-th definable real. Claiming r is in the enumeration is refutable.
assumptions: Diagonal construction differs at every index
constraints: k is a valid enumeration index

results.name: Burali-Forti Paradox
results.statement: The ordinal number of all ordinals must be greater than itself.
results.formal_proposition: Strict well-ordering on ordinals is irreflexive (not alpha < alpha). Supposing the class of all ordinals is a set with ordinal Omega forces Omega < Omega, refuting sethood.
assumptions: Ordinals are well-ordered by strict membership
Every set of ordinals has an upper bound ordinal

results.name: Cantor Paradox
results.statement: Power set of universal set must have strictly greater cardinality than universal set.
results.formal_proposition: For universal set U, |P(U)| <= |U|. Cantor theorem proves |U| < |P(U)|. The conjunction is refutable.
assumptions: Power set operation is valid on U
axioms: Subsets of universal set belong to universal set

results.name: Sorites Paradox
results.statement: Removing one grain from a heap leaves a heap; by induction one grain is a heap.
results.formal_proposition: Crisp induction on bounded tolerance boundary (heap(n) => heap(n-1)) forces heap(1) from heap(5), refuting the negative boundary condition.

results.name: Ship of Theseus
results.statement: Gradual replacement of every part raises persistent identity ambiguity.
results.formal_proposition: Identity transitivity requires that if continuous ship A = B and reconstructed ship A = C, then B = C. Asserting B != C refutes classical equivalence.
assumptions: Original material reassembly preserves identity (A = C)
constraints: A, B, C are distinct token states

results.name: Grandfather Paradox
results.statement: Time traveler prevents own lineage, invalidating the travel premise.
results.formal_proposition: Lineage consistency: Time travel T requires traveler birth B (T => B). Travel execution action causes not(B) (T => not B). Asserting T yields contradiction B and not B.

results.name: Bootstrap Paradox
results.statement: An object or information is sent back in time, creating uncaused existence.
results.formal_proposition: Classical strict causal orders are irreflexive (not causes(x, x)). An uncaused ontological time-loop asserting causes(e, e) is refutable.
assumptions: Causality is a strict partial order
Ontological loop event e causes itself
axioms: Irreflexivity and transitivity of strict causality

results.name: Raven Paradox (Hempel)
results.statement: Observing a green apple confirms "All ravens are black" via contrapositive.
results.formal_proposition: Universal implication (forall x: Raven(x) => Black(x)) is logically equivalent to its contrapositive (forall x: not Black(x) => not Raven(x)). Non-equivalence is refutable.

results.name: Goodman New Riddle of Induction (Grue)
results.statement: Predicate "grue" (green before t, blue after) equally supported by evidence.
results.formal_proposition: Simultaneous projection of color predicates: At future time t_future, an object cannot be simultaneously green and blue under mutually exclusive color categories.
assumptions: Green and Blue are disjoint color predicates
Grue definition shifts at time threshold t
axioms: Mutual exclusivity of fundamental color terms
constraints: is_green and is_blue cannot both be true

results.name: Newcomb Problem
results.statement: Superintelligent predictor: choose One Box ($1M) or Two Boxes ($1M + $1K).
results.formal_proposition: Dominance principle dictates choosing two boxes while Expected Utility under perfect prediction dictates choosing one box. Simultaneous single-choice satisfaction is refutable.
assumptions: Expected utility under perfect predictor: choose one box
axioms: Exclusive decision choice between one and two boxes

results.name: Prisoner Dilemma
results.statement: Dominant individual strategy leads to suboptimal collective outcome.
results.formal_proposition: Strict dominance equilibrium (Defect, Defect) with payoff 1 strictly less than mutual cooperation payoff 3. Refuting that Nash equilibrium is Pareto optimal.

results.name: Simpson Paradox
results.statement: Trend appears in groups but reverses when groups are aggregated.
results.formal_proposition: Subgroup success rate reversal upon aggregation: a1 > b1 and a2 > b2 while totalA < totalB is mathematically SATISFIABLE.

results.name: Monty Hall Problem
results.statement: Switching doors doubles win probability from 1/3 to 2/3.
results.formal_proposition: Conditional probability update: P(win | stay) = 1/3 while P(win | switch) = 2/3. Refuting the intuitive claim that switching and staying have equal 1/2 probability.

results.name: Birthday Paradox
results.statement: In 23 people, >50% chance of a shared birthday.
results.formal_proposition: Combinatorial collision product: For n=23 and days=365, complementary probability Q(23) <= 0.493, yielding P(collision) > 0.5. Refuting P(collision) <= 0.5.

results.name: Banach-Tarski Paradox
results.statement: A solid ball can be decomposed into 5 non-measurable sets and reassembled into two.
results.formal_proposition: Under finite additivity of Lebesgue measure, measurable decomposition of volume V preserves total volume V. Reassembly into 2V is refutable for measurable subsets.

results.name: Gabriel Horn (Torricelli Trumpet)
results.statement: Surface of revolution has infinite surface area but finite volume (pi).
results.formal_proposition: Volume integral V = pi * int_1^inf (1/x^2) dx = pi is finite, whereas surface area integral A >= 2pi * int_1^inf (1/x) dx diverges. Conjunction of finite volume with bounded surface area is refutable.
assumptions: Solid of revolution for y = 1/x on [1, inf)
axioms: Divergence of harmonic integral for p=1

results.name: Olbers Paradox
results.statement: In an infinite static universe, the night sky should be uniformly bright.
results.formal_proposition: In infinite static Euclidean space with uniform star number density, integrated flux diverges. Conjunction of infinite static universe with finite sky flux is refutable.

results.name: Fermi Paradox
results.statement: High probability of extraterrestrial life vs total absence of observational contact.
results.formal_proposition: Drake expectation N >> 1 with unhindered interstellar colonization implies observed civilizations > 0. The conjunction of high expected colonization with observed = 0 is refutable.
assumptions: Drake equation parameters yield large N

results.name: Twin Paradox
results.statement: Traveling twin accelerates away and returns younger than stationary twin.
results.formal_proposition: Asymmetric Minkowski spacetime proper time: tau_traveler = T * sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) < T. Refuting hypothesis that traveling twin elapsed proper time equals stationary twin.
assumptions: Minkowski metric interval ds^2 = c^2 dt^2 - dx^2

results.name: EPR Paradox
results.statement: Entangled particles exhibit instantaneous correlations ("spooky action at a distance").
results.formal_proposition: Bell CHSH theorem: Local hidden variable realism bounds correlation |S| <= 2. Quantum entangled state yields S = 2*sqrt(2) approx 2.828. Quantum correlation violating classical bound is refutable under local realism.

results.name: Schrodinger Cat Paradox
results.statement: Quantum superposition entangled with macroscopic feline life state.
results.formal_proposition: Decoherence through environment-induced superselection forces macroscopic interference terms to 0. Macroscopic persistent interference (> 0.1) is refutable.
assumptions: Macroscopic pointer state entanglement with environment
Trace over unobserved degrees of freedom
axioms: Decoherence theorem in open quantum systems

results.name: Zeno Arrow Paradox
results.statement: At every instant of time, a flying arrow occupies a space equal to itself and is motionless.
results.formal_proposition: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the limit dx/dt as dt -> 0. Non-zero velocity v0 > 0 refutes the claim that instantaneous occupancy implies zero velocity.
assumptions: Arrow has position trajectory x(t) = v0 * t with v0 > 0

results.name: Zeno Dichotomy Paradox
results.statement: Motion can never start because one must traverse infinite half-intervals first.
results.formal_proposition: Sum of geometric intervals sum_{n=1}^inf (1/2^n) = 1 converges in finite time t0. Refuting that traversing infinite half-intervals diverges.

results.name: Braess Paradox
results.statement: Adding a road to a congested traffic network can increase overall travel times.
results.formal_proposition: In a congested network with non-cooperative routing, adding a shortcut edge creates a new user equilibrium with higher latency. This phenomenon is SATISFIABLE.

results.name: Byzantine Generals Paradox
results.statement: Reaching consensus across unreliable networks with traitorous nodes.
results.formal_proposition: Lamport-Shostak-Pease Theorem: Synchronous Byzantine agreement with m traitorous nodes requires strictly > 3m nodes (n >= 3m + 1). For n=3 and m=1, reaching consensus is refutable.
assumptions: Oral message model without digital signatures
